title: Ashwani Kumar v. State of U.P.
coram: Vineet Saran, J. and B. Amit Sthalekar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; no tenant connection without considering landlord objection.
headnote: A landlord alleged that occupants claiming tenancy were seeking a new connection without his no-objection. Disposing of the writ at the threshold, and recording the licensee's statement that a tenanted-premises connection requires the landlord's no-objection under the Supply Code, the Court directed the Executive Engineer not to grant supply to those occupants without first considering the landlord's pending objection.
facts: The petitioner, owner of the property, alleged that respondents 4 and 5 were seeking a new electricity connection from the Urban Distribution Division at Moradabad as his tenants, without his no-objection. He contended that the Supply Code did not permit a tenant connection without the landlord's consent, and had objected to the Executive Engineer, Vidyut Nagariya Vitran Khand (First), Moradabad, on 28 June 2013. Counsel for the corporation stated that a connection in tenanted premises could be granted only after the landlord's no-objection. Private respondents were not noticed.

holding_units.holding: The distribution licensee shall not grant an electricity connection to persons claiming tenancy of the petitioner's premises without first considering the landlord's objection already filed before the Executive Engineer.
holding_units.flag: Order cites the Electricity Supply Code generally for landlord no-objection on tenanted premises; no clause number is given.

not_decided.point: Merits of the landlord's objection and whether the occupants were entitled to a connection
not_decided.note: The Court did not decide whether a landlord's no-objection is a mandatory condition under the Supply Code, nor whether respondents 4 and 5 could be given supply; that was left to the Executive Engineer.
